biography.plain_text: Dmitry Medvedev is a Russian lawyer and politician who served as president from 2008 to 2012 and prime minister from 2012 to 2020. Since leaving the premiership, he has served as deputy chairman of the Security Council, continuing a public career that began in St Petersburg's municipal administration during the 1990s.
biography.html: Dmitry Medvedev is a Russian lawyer and politician who served as president from 2008 to 2012 and prime minister from 2012 to 2020. Since leaving the premiership, he has served as deputy chairman of the Security Council, continuing a public career that began in St Petersburg's municipal administration during the 1990s.

confidence.reason: Official Kremlin and Security Council sources establish the municipal-government start, presidency, premiership and current appointment; Forbes and AP independently corroborate the same political identity and office sequence.

long_biography.plain_text:
Before entering national politics, Dmitry Medvedev studied law at Leningrad State University, completed postgraduate work and lectured there for most of the 1990s. He also advised St Petersburg's municipal government and chaired Gazprom's board through much of the following decade.

Medvedev moved into the federal presidential administration at the end of the decade, later becoming chief of staff and first deputy prime minister. He won the presidential election in 2008, served one term, and then led the government as prime minister for nearly eight years. In 2020 he was appointed to the newly created post of deputy chairman of the Security Council, where he remains a permanent member.
